newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds up to new high on brokers upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds up to new high on brokers upgrades.

text.p: Shares in banking group Lloyds TSB Plc, boosted this week by Abbey National Plc's decision to raise mortagage rates, hit another record high on Wednesday after two brokers upgraded profit estimates, dealers said.
By 0945 GMT, Lloyds shares were up 6p at 429p.
NatWest Securities put out a strong buy recommendation on the stock after upping profit estimates for 1996 and 1997. Dealers said HSBC James Capel had also upgraded forecasts.
NatWest raised its 1996 pre-tax profit forecast to 2,502 million stg from 2,386 million, while 1997 figures were up to 2,920 million stg from 2,765 million.

Dealers said HSBC James Capel had raised its figures to 2.498 billion stg for 1996 and 2.956 billion for 1997 and repeated a "buy" recommendation on the stock, but analysts at the brokerage denied any change. The upgrades were based on good cost control and falling exposure to bad debt, traders said.
"The stock has been under pressure for technical reasons but now that is out of the way," one said. --Brian Killen, London Newsroom 44 171 542 7972
